title: Al-Idrisi's world: the map made for Roger II of Sicily, set against a modern one
excerpt: In 1154 a Muslim geographer in Palermo drew the known world for the Norman king of Sicily, south at the top. I read 431 of its towns and measured it: directions right to a median 10 degrees, and Sicily drawn best and biggest of all.
seo_description: Al-Idrisi's 1154 world map beside a modern one: 431 towns, seven climates, Sicily drawn best, and a test against the Hereford map.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Al-Idrisi's World' in black and blue on pale paper, beside Konrad Miller's reconstruction of al-Idrisi's map as drawn, with south at the top, and a small modern map of Europe, North Africa and Asia dotted with 431 coloured towns. Text: the map made for Roger II of Sicily in 1154, south at the top, set against a modern one.
